analysis:
This PR changes only docs/provider/cli-reference.md. It bumps the last-updated date, adds a paragraph (head lines 443-447) on drain completion without a coordinator acknowledgement, and adds a runtime-constants row for the coordinator handshake deadline (head ~1943; its table row is not visible in the head excerpt, only in the patch and the base-side runtime-constants table). No executable code, keys, authorization or encryption logic changes. The two units supplied were the base text from line 1726 and the head text from line 1 to 397, so the changed head ranges near 443-447 and ~1943 are visible only through the patch excerpt. Findings must cite visible lines, so I did not cite them.

Security-relevant reading of the doc claims:
- Drain without acknowledgement: this applies only when no work is left and no registered coordinator session exists. The doc states that a registered session must still acknowledge before the deadline. This is a lifecycle and availability semantic for the CLI. It touches the T-053 and TB-002 areas only loosely, and I found no doc-stated weakening of authorization, receipts or revocation. Whether the code treats 'no registered session' correctly, so a connected provider cannot skip the acknowledgement, is an implementation contract outside the supplied evidence. The next pass should check ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift (performLifecycleDrain) if code is in scope.
- The 30 s handshake deadline with reconnect backoff is an availability hardening that mitigates a stalled-connection DoS (TB-002). It is documentation only here, and its implementation file is not supplied.

The retained base content (cache storage, T-041 details, logout, App Attest passthrough) is unchanged. The doc still states the prefix cache, App Attest worker flag, and fan-helper constants consistently with the threat model. No regression or new attack surface is identified in the visible text. The patch excerpt is truncated, so unseen changes are possible but unverified.
